rationale:
Evidence: iteration 8 (score 708.5) is the best raced design. Oval (20/20) and s-bend (20/20) now finish reliably. Slalom is still 0/20, but its progress rose from 0.41 to 0.56 when the sensors moved from y=0.05 to y=0.07, and its steering_oscillation fell from 0.30 to 0.26. Lead distance is therefore still the lever that helps, and it has not yet added jitter. Mean rms_error stays near 0.02 on slalom, so the robot tracks on average and leaves the line at sudden alternating bends, which points to late turn-in correction. Raising kp was ruled out: in iteration 4, kp 3.7 hurt slalom and s-bend. Changing kd or base_speed would be a second variable, so I am not changing them.

Change (one variable): sensor y moves from 0.07 to 0.08 m, the upper limit of the allowed range. Sensor x positions (-0.04 to 0.04, spacing 0.02, 16 mm footprints), kp 3.0, kd 0.8, ki 0.02, base_speed 1.3, mass 0.6 kg, wheel geometry and last_direction line loss all stay the same, so the look-ahead effect can be read directly against iteration 8.

Expected result: slalom max_error falls further, and slalom progress rises from 0.56 toward 0.7 or higher, with some slalom completions possible. Oval and s-bend should keep finishing. Because sensor y is at its limit, this is the last look-ahead step available.

Hypotheses and checks: (a) If slalom still exits at max_error near 0.06 with no progress gain, steering authority is the limit, so the next step is kp near 3.3 with kd held. (b) If oval completion drops below 20/20 (the lead overshoots on straights), y should return to about 0.07. (c) If steering_oscillation rises above 0.35 on slalom, kd should drop toward 0.6.

Measurements wanted: all per-track metrics (completion, progress, completion_time, rms_error, max_error, line_loss_events, steering_oscillation, control_effort, noise_robustness), so the look-ahead effect can be read separately for oval, s-bend and slalom.
